tokens.v: EXTREME MACRO — the frame filled by a hand's width of the jacket's shoulder laid over a freshly cleaved slate face after a late-autumn downpour; no body anywhere in frame, so no wardrobe reads at this crop. The hard seam where the chalk-white yoke meets storm-slate runs a diagonal corner to corner, welded tape reading proud under the face fabric, rain runnels crossing the slate's fracture steps beneath it. 100mm macro at f/5.6, framed 1:1 life-size, camera square to the shoulder plane: the ripstop grid legible, beads standing tall and round on the treated face, one pinned in the channel of the seam, the slate's mica firing cold points at the edges. A wet slate flake crosses the top-left corner out of focus. SLATE HARBOR is a bonded reflective transfer on the white yoke just above the seam, a hair proud of the fabric and dead flat grey in the ambient — a small hard source sitting right beside the lens goes near-axis on it and the letters burn pure white while the storm-slate around them stays matte and unlit, beads sliding off the sealed film to gather along its lower edge.
